ruling.recommended_action: Send to Ryde ops / expedited human review for the RD-5 scope question on segment F3 (Balestier Road consent vs driven path). The reviewer should decide the exemption, and if the segment is not exempt issue a voucher of $6.90 to the rider ($23.84 ÷ 16.91 km = $1.4098/km; 4.89 km × $1.4098/km = $6.90); do not refund the $0.11 metered waiting fee. No account action against the driver on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
Factual summary for the reviewer: RydeTAXI metered trip Junction 8 → Tanjong Pagar Centre, 21:18–21:46, an 11.6 km optimal route but 16.9 km actually driven (+5.3 km, +46%) [F1], charged $36.67 [F7]. One off-route segment is code-settled: 21:26–21:37, 6.64 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.76 km, adding 4.89 km and straying up to 2,070 m off the optimal route [F3][RD-2].

RD-4 gives no exemption: no traffic incident was recorded on the route during the trip window [F15], and the only congestion record, the Central Expressway at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 21:06–21:26 [F12], is a band fact that is corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment on its own [RD-4]. The other traffic facts (Bishan Street 11, Braddell Road) are unrelated corridors [F13][F14].

The undecidable element is the scope of the rider's consent [RD-5]. Consent in form is the rider's own timestamped message, sent before the segment: at 21:23 the driver asked "Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Balestier Road?" [F8] and at 21:24 the rider replied "Can lah, go ahead." [F9][F10]; this is not the driver's after-the-fact statement [F11]. But the message answers a proposal naming one road, Balestier Road — a specific named-road consent, which under RD-5 covers driving on Balestier Road only and requires the record to tie the segment to that road. Nothing does: no gps, traffic or chat fact names Balestier Road for the driven path [F3][F11][F12][F13][F14], and the fact table carries no road names for the track. Timing alone is not correspondence [F3][F8][F9][RD-5/G13]. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either, so the finding is undetermined, not counts [RD-5]. That undetermined finding drives the amount, so the case goes to a person rather than being auto-executed.

Amount, if the reviewer holds the segment unexempt: $23.84 ÷ 16.91 km = $1.4098/km [F4][F7]; 4.89 km × $1.4098/km = $6.8959 → $6.90 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The residual slip to the billed 5.35 km and the $0.11 metered waiting charge [F4][F5] stay with the rider: RD-2 refunds only unexempt-segment extra km, and RD-3(c) charges metered waiting time on RydeTAXI [RD-2][RD-3]. No ERP/toll or unpublished item appears in the breakdown [F7][FARE-1].

Flag: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F18], so RD-6's "repeated" condition is not met and no account action is required [RD-6]. Safety: the chat is two ordinary routing messages [F8][F9], the driver's statement is a route account [F11], the complaint is a fare question, weather fair [F16], no incident logged [F15] — no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving material [SAFE-1]. Evidence is otherwise complete (timestamped chat, measured segment, fare breakdown) [F3][F4][F7][F10].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own timestamped message sent before the segment [F9] answers the driver's 21:23 proposal naming one road, Balestier Road [F8], so under RD-5 the consent is a specific named-road consent covering driving on Balestier Road only. No fact ties the 21:26–21:37 driven track to Balestier Road (the traffic facts name the Central Expressway, Bishan Street 11 and Braddell Road [F12][F13][F14]; the driver's statement names the road only as his question [F11]), and timing alone is not correspondence [RD-5/G13]; nothing places the segment elsewhere either, so the finding is undetermined rather than counts. RD-4 does not exempt it: no qualifying incident and a speed band alone is corroborative only [F15][F12][RD-4]. This finding drives the amount ($6.90 if unexempt: 4.89 km × $1.4098/km [F3][F4][RD-2]), so a person decides.

rejected_claims.reason: The 4.89 km extra-distance segment is code-settled as an off-route segment [F3][RD-1], but whether it is an unexempt deviation requires the RD-3/RD-5 review, which is undetermined because the record does not tie the driven track to the consented road [F8][F9][F11][RD-5]; the amount therefore cannot be auto-computed from C1 alone.

The absence of a fact tying the segment to Balestier Road [F3][F14][F11] is accepted as the ground of the undetermined finding under RD-5/G13, but it does not itself convert the segment into a refundable 'counts' finding: the record neither ties the segment to the named road nor places it elsewhere, so a person decides [RD-5].

The rider's pre-segment message is accepted in form [F9][F8][F10], but under RD-5 a specific named-road consent covers driving on the named road only and the record must tie the segment to it; nothing does [F3][F11][F12][F13][F14], so the segment is not exempt outright and the requested no_action is not granted [RD-5].

The Central Expressway band-2 record [F12] cannot justify the reroute: RD-4(a) needs an incident on the replaced stretch and none was recorded [F15], and under RD-4(b) a band alone is corroborative only [RD-4].

Accepted that no ERP/toll or unpublished surcharge appears in the breakdown [F7], so FARE-1/FARE-2 add nothing; but that does not dispose of the metered excess distance, which is the disputed item under RD-2 [F4][RD-2].
Accepted: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F18], so RD-6's 'repeated' condition is not met and no flag_account is added on this record [RD-6].
